content.title: Spring Equinox Friday: Exact Time The Seasons Change
content.text: ToplineWhat day is the first day of spring 2026? Friday, March 20, sees the vernal (spring) equinox, which marks the beginning of astronomical spring in the Northern Hemisphere and astronomical fall in the Southern Hemisphere. Equinoxes and solstices happen twice a year. Here’s everything you need to know about when they are in 2026 — and what they mean. What day is the first day of spring 2026? Friday, March 20, sees the vernal (spring) equinox. gettyKey FactsThis year’s spring equinox will occur on Friday, March 20, at precisely 14:46 UTC, according to TimeAndDate.com. This equinox occurs when the sun crosses above Earth’s equator while traveling from south to north, according to NASA. The planet experiences equal amounts of sunlight, so approximately 12 hours of day and 12 hours of night, on the days around the March and September equinoxes. Equi means ‘equal’ and nox means ‘night’ in Latin. Just after sunset on Friday, March 20, a delicate crescent moon will be seen very close to Venus in the west-southwest. Earth's annual journey around the sun — while rotating on a titled axis — explains the seasons. The equinoxes and solstices are the waymarkers.gettySpring Equinox ExplainedThe March equinox sees the sun directly above the equator at midday, shining in the constellation Pisces. Earth rotates on an axis tilted by 23.4 degrees as it orbits the sun, with the consequence being that each hemisphere receives different amounts of sunlight throughout the year. This causes the seasons.March’s equinox is called the spring equinox in the Northern Hemisphere because it marks the point in Earth’s orbit when this region of the planet begins to receive more hours of sunlight than darkness, so it begins to warm up. In the Southern Hemisphere, the March equinox has the opposite effect. As the region starts to tilt away from the sun, summer ends and fall begins.Exact Times For The Spring Equinox In All U.s. Timezones14:46 UTC on Friday, March 20 — the start of spring — translates to these times in North America:10:46 a.m. EDT.9:46 a.m. CDT.8:46 a.m. MDT.7:46 a.m. PDT.6:46 a.m. AKDT (Alaska).4:46 a.m. HST (Hawaii).The March equinox is always on March 19, 20 or 21, and the September equinox happens on Sept. 21, 22, 23 or 24. Dates For Solstices And Equinoxes In 2026Equinoxes mark the moments when the sun crosses the celestial equator, while solstices mark the days when Earth’s axis is tilted toward or away from the sun. This creates the longest day in one hemisphere and the longest night in the other.The next solstice — the summer solstice in the Northern Hemisphere and the winter solstice in the Southern Hemisphere — will happen on Sunday, June 21.The September (fall) equinox will happen on Tuesday, Sept. 22, and the December (winter) solstice on Monday, Dec. 21.
